title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is an insider misuse case, not a model failure. The systems involved, a Flock camera network, a tag reader system and the Georgia Crime Information Center database, were built and authorised for law enforcement queries, and the alleged misuse was a sworn officer running those queries for personal reasons. The failure sits at the point of access, where a legitimate credential was used for a purpose outside the one the system was deployed for.

The controls that would have caught it are query auditing and purpose logging, not model accuracy. Nothing in the reporting says whether such oversight existed, whether any alert fired, or how the conduct came to investigators' attention. The account states only that he was terminated when the investigation began, which places the detection after the fact rather than at the moment of the queries.

The charges are allegations. An indictment is not a conviction, and the counts of oath violation, computer invasion of privacy, prohibited use of captured license plate data and stalking have not been proven. Whether the tracking occurred as described, and what evidence supports it, is not established by the reporting summarised here.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A former Coffee County sheriff’s deputy, Chris Ashley Rozar, 49, was released on bond after a grand jury indicted him on eight counts, including four counts of violation of oath by a public officer, two counts of computer invasion of privacy, one count of prohibited use of captured license plate data, and one count of stalking. Investigators say he misused the sheriff’s office Flock camera system, tag reader system, and the Georgia Crime Information Center database for personal reasons between April and May 2024. He was terminated when the investigation began.

The woman he is accused of tracking spoke anonymously, saying she hopes her story encourages other women to report abuse. She waited two years for the GBI investigation to finish. Rozar was arrested on May 5 and released on bond the same day. His arraignment is scheduled for May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court.
